No docs sentence; inspection of stage-4 flutter_bootstrap.js: load() starts the renderer (`l.renderer==="canvaskit"?d.canvasKit=I(d,r,f,h)`) and injects the main.dart.js script; the default callback is `a.initializeEngine(t).then(l=>l.runApp())`, so both must arrive before runApp and any frame. The service worker shipped is a stub that unregisters itself, so nothing is cached for a first visit.

RFC 9110 §12.5.3: "When sent by a user agent in a request, Accept-Encoding indicates the content codings acceptable in a response." §8.4: "The \"Content-Encoding\" header field indicates what content codings have been applied to the representation ... and thus what decoding mechanisms have to be applied in order to obtain data in the media type referenced by the Content-Type header field."

Caddy encode page: "If omitted, `zstd` (preferred) and `gzip` are enabled by default." Encoding chosen from Accept-Encoding; "if the client has no strong preference (q-factor), then the first supported encoding is used." Default match includes application/javascript* and application/wasm*. Capture: all five files `(zstd)`, while `wc -c` on disk still gives raw sizes. Lesson section 3 now carries the q-factor condition.

issues.quote: Chromium is the browser engine inside Chrome, Edge and similar browsers
issues.text: New in changed text. Chromium is the open-source browser that Chrome and Edge are built on; the engine the loader tests for is Blink (flutter_bootstrap.js: hasImageCodecs requires browserEngine blink). Calling Chromium 'the browser engine' conflates the two.
issues.fix: Write: "Chromium is the open-source browser that Chrome, Edge and similar browsers are built on; they take `canvaskit/chromium/`, other browsers take `canvaskit/`."
